Data Storage & External Services

UseMockData is true in the checked-in Web.config, so the default runtime uses an in-memory catalog service. If this setting is disabled, Entity Framework 6 uses the configured SQL Server LocalDB connection. Application Insights modules provide telemetry; no other external service integration was identified.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Server-rendered Web Forms pages and their code-behind form the presentation layer; there is no separate API gateway or REST service.
  • Autofac selects either the singleton mock catalog service or a per-request-scope database service based on configuration.
  • Entity Framework 6 maps catalog items to required brand and type references.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem is the mutable catalog data object used by the page code-behind and service. PaginatedItemsViewModel is the page response model; route values supply pagination and item identifiers. CatalogBrand and CatalogType provide reference data. No separate request/response DTOs, OpenAPI/Swagger documents, protobuf schemas, or GraphQL schemas were found. Communication to the browser is server-rendered HTML rather than JSON.

Communication Patterns

  • Synchronous: Web Forms page handlers call ICatalogService directly. CatalogService calls Entity Framework 6 and LocalDB when database mode is selected.
  • Default mode: UseMockData=true selects CatalogServiceMock, which serves an in-memory list.
  • Asynchronous messaging and resilience: No message broker, retry policy, circuit breaker, or service discovery client was identified.
  • Gateway and aggregation: There is no API gateway or cross-service response aggregation.
  • Startup dependencies: ASP.NET application startup registers routes, bundles, and Autofac; database initialization is configured only when mock data is disabled. See configuration-inventory.md for configuration details.
  • Security posture: No API-level authentication, authorization, or TLS configuration was identified in the application configuration. The site uses page routes and postbacks, not secured service contracts.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing and maintaining a product catalog. Catalog items are associated with a brand and a type, with stock and pricing information presented to users.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogA listed product, including price, picture reference, and stock thresholdsBelongs to one CatalogBrand and one CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalogA maker or label associated with productsHas many CatalogItems
CatalogTypeCatalogA classification for productsHas many CatalogItems

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopLegacyWebForms / ICatalogServiceCatalogCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeNone in mock mode; LocalDB through EF6 when mock mode is disabled

The application is a single bounded context. No inter-service data exchange or cross-context aggregation was found.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse and view catalog items

The default page requests a page of catalog items and binds the returned data to the Web Forms list. Selecting a product opens its details page. Pagination is driven by the route's index and size values; the service orders items by identifier and returns the selected page.

Workflow 2: Create a catalog item

The user submits the create form. Required-name and numeric range validators run, and the page checks model state before constructing a CatalogItem. The catalog service assigns an identifier and persists the item, then redirects to the catalog list. In mock mode, the identifier is based on the current maximum; in database mode, the Hi/Lo generator obtains identifiers from a SQL sequence.

Workflow 3: Update or delete a catalog item

The edit and delete pages load an item by route identifier. A valid edit replaces the catalog item through the service; a delete postback removes it. Both successful operations redirect to the catalog list.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No cross-service calls or data composition flows were identified. In database mode, EF6 loads a catalog item together with its brand and type references. In the default mock mode, CatalogServiceMock composes those references from in-memory catalog lists.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User as "Catalog User" participant Page as "Create.aspx" participant Service as "ICatalogService" participant Mock as "CatalogServiceMock" participant EF as "Entity Framework 6" participant DB as "SQL Server LocalDB" User->>Page: Submit catalog item form Page->>Page: Validate required name and numeric ranges alt Input is invalid Page-->>User: Show validation errors else Input is valid Page->>Service: CreateCatalogItem(item) alt UseMockData is true Service->>Mock: Assign next in-memory ID and add item Mock-->>Service: Item added else UseMockData is false Service->>EF: Allocate ID and save item EF->>DB: Insert catalog record DB-->>EF: Save completed EF-->>Service: Item saved end Service-->>Page: Creation completed Page-->>User: Redirect to catalog list end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • A catalog item's name is required on the create and edit forms.
  • The form constrains price to a non-negative value up to 1,000,000 and stock, restock, and maximum-stock values to 0–10,000,000.
  • The entity model applies range and price-format validation to numeric catalog fields.
  • Items reference an existing brand and type; the EF model requires both relationships.
  • A successful create, update, or delete saves the corresponding service operation and returns the user to the catalog list.
  • Each database-mode write is persisted through EF6 SaveChanges; no cross-service transaction or compensation flow was identified.

Entity Model

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are defined under src/eShopLegacyWebForms/Models/. CatalogDBContext maps them to Catalog, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType, respectively. Catalog items require a brand and type; identifiers for catalog items are generated through the Hi/Lo sequence path in database mode.

Caching Strategy

No explicit cache provider, cache regions, or time-to-live settings were found. CatalogServiceMock stores its catalog in a singleton in-memory list; this is the selected data implementation under the default configuration, not a read-through or cache-aside layer. ASP.NET session state is configured in-process but is used for session metadata rather than catalog caching.

Data Ownership Boundaries

All catalog entities are owned by this single application. In database mode, one EF6 context provides access to all three tables; in mock mode, one in-memory catalog list is used. There are no cross-service database calls, separate service databases, or CQRS read/write stores.
